anchors.reason: The dataset README names this Nature Neuroscience article (Starkweather et al. 2026) as the source article. Its authors, six SEEG patients, and OFC approach-avoidance task match the dataset.

metadata.methods_description: Patients with stereotactic depth electrodes (five at UCSF, one at WUSTL) performed an approach-avoidance task. SEEG signals were bipolar re-referenced, band-pass filtered at 0.5-200 Hz and notch filtered at 60 Hz and harmonics. HFA (70-150 Hz) was computed as the mean of ten 10-Hz sub-band Hilbert envelopes, each normalised to a 10 s pre-task baseline. Data were epoched per trial at 1 kHz and aligned to trial onset or decision.

citation_details.title: Mapping reward processing circuits: the orbitofrontal-nucleus accumbens white matter pathways and their associations to psychopathological traits
citation_details.author: Santiago Mezzano, Fedal Saini, Veronica Orbecchi, Tobías Fernández‐Borkel, Manu Raghavan, Mustafa Okan Irfanoglu, Ahmad Beyh, Flavio Dell’Acqua
citation_details.abstract: Abstract Dysfunctions in reward circuits, including projections from the orbitofrontal cortex (OFC) to the nucleus accumbens (NAcc), have been implicated in psychopathology. The OFC is functionally divided into the medial OFC (mOFC), which processes rewards, and the lateral OFC (lOFC), which responds to non-reward or punishment stimuli. We investigated the structural connectivity of the lOFC-NAcc and mOFC-NAcc pathways and their associations with psychopathological traits using tractography-defined ROI analysis. Diffusion-weighted imaging data from 165 participants (aged 22 - 35, 53% male) in the Human Connectome Project (HCP) were analysed using spherical deconvolution tractography. MegaTrack, a novel tool, enabled tract segmentation via a single manual dissection mapped back to native space.
